rationale: Implementation (composite algebraic rewrite inside PyTorch eager, torch.nn.functional.conv2d, FP32 cudnn under the workload's frozen policies: TF32 off, cudnn.benchmark off): each of the 20 selected conv->BatchNorm2d epilogue sites (17 ResNetConvLayer modules incl. the embedder, 3 ResNetShortCut modules; 9 sites with trailing nn.ReLU, 8 with nn.Identity, 3 shortcuts without a third child) is replaced at the module call site by one fused convolution: s = gamma/sqrt(running_var+eps) per output channel, W_fold = W*s, b_fold = beta - s*running_mean (+ s*conv_bias if a conv bias existed; all 20 observed convs are bias-less), then the site's original activation (ReLU or identity). Scale/shift are computed in float64 and stored as new contiguous FP32 tensors during build; the model's parameters, buffers and module tree are never mutated. Each replacement takes the original forward's args/kwargs (without self), applies the fused path only when the input matches the observed shape/stride/dtype/device signature, and otherwise falls back to the module's original bound forward captured at build time (before installation), so unobserved inputs keep exact parent semantics. Objective is wall-clock latency_ms of the frozen batch=1 FP32 ResNet-18 forward (TF32/cudnn-benchmark disabled, atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1), so only structure-preserving rewrites of the observed execution are eligible; this attempt implements the joint selection's primary hypothesis: fold all 20 eval-mode BatchNorm affines into their preceding convolutions. The edits are mutually dependent and therefore installed as one mapping: rescaling conv weights while keeping the BN would corrupt logits, and removing the BN without folding would corrupt logits; only the closed transform (per-channel weight rescale, folded conv bias, BN dropped) preserves semantics, which is why all 20 sites are replaced together. Folding is placed at the ResNetConvLayer/ResNetShortCut module boundary (the parents of the conv and batch_norm call groups in the selection) rather than at the aten operator boundary: it removes, per site, the Sequential child dispatch, the Conv2d module dispatch, the BatchNorm2d module dispatch, the F.batch_norm->aten dispatch, the 20 aten.batch_norm kernels (43.84us, 6.0% of the 731.39us diagnostic CUDA total, plus launch/dispatch overhead a wall-latency metric charges), and the separate ReLU module dispatch for ConvLayer sites, while the 20 aten.conv2d invocations still execute (now from inside the fused forward, with unchanged input/weight shapes, strides and dtypes, so the same aten call paths remain observable). No aten-level replacements are returned, which also rules out any double-application of the fold through operator interception. inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so this is the first attempt with no prior measured feedback to incorporate. The transform is algebraically exact for training=False, track_running_stats=True BatchNorm; the only deviation is FP32 rounding of the folded weights/bias and cudnn's conv+bias epilogue versus a separate BN kernel. Local CPU verification on the real ResNet-18 config (all 20 sites replaced, non-trivial affine and running statistics, full-model forward) measured max relative logits deviation 2.1e-7 and identical top-1, roughly three orders of magnitude inside the quality gate; GPU accumulation will differ slightly but with large margin. Expected wall-latency effect is a hypothesis to be A/B measured by the framework, not an assumed fact: kernel-time savings and removed launches/dispatches only translate to latency_ms if they sit on the critical path. The selection's secondary sub-hypothesis (a shape-preserving FP32 call-path/layout variant for the stage-3 conv sites, especially the 115.97us 256->512 stride-2 call and the 3x 512@7x7 calls) is deliberately deferred to a later attempt: it cannot be tuned without the bound worker's measured feedback, and bundling an unmeasured layout change would risk the whole candidate against the same tolerance gate. Eliminated-call validity: the consumers of every eliminated call are the site's own activation (recomputed inside the fused forward where present) and the downstream residual add_/ReLU/pooler/classifier, which consume the fused output tensor of identical shape, dtype, device and contiguity; the residual adds, BasicLayer activations, pooling and classifier are outside the selected boundary and execute unchanged. State lifecycle: model parameters and BN running stats are invariant after prepare for this inference-only workload (adapter.reset only calls .eval() and resets memory counters), so the build-time fold remains valid for warm-model reuse; eval-mode BN performs no running-stat updates, so skipping it changes no state. No fixture-dependent outputs are cached: the full workload executes on every invocation.
setup_work: At build time, for each of the 20 sites: read conv weight and BN gamma/beta/running_mean/running_var/eps from the live modules, compute per-channel scale/shift in float64, produce one contiguous FP32 folded weight (and one folded bias vector) per site, and capture the module's original bound forward plus the observed input signature for fallback. Total setup is ~40 small device-side elementwise kernels and a few Python-ms; no synchronization or stream changes are required, and it happens once during build, outside the timed region. Memory: the folded copies replicate the conv weights (11,171,488 FP32 elements, ~44.7 MiB) plus 3,968 bias floats (~15.5 KiB); original parameters and buffers remain resident, so steady-state GPU memory increases by about 45 MiB. Per-forward peak activation memory is unchanged or slightly reduced (each site's fused conv output is written once and consumed in place of the previous conv-output/BN-output pair, and no extra workspace beyond cudnn's usual conv workspace is introduced).
quality_risks: FP32 rounding of the folded weights/bias and the cudnn conv+bias epilogue versus a separate batch_norm kernel make logits deviate slightly from the reference (CPU end-to-end check on the real structure: max_rel 2.1e-7, top-1 identical); the framework's atol=rtol=1e-4 plus exact-top-1 gate is the acceptance test, and any failure triggers atomic fallback to the unmodified execution.

The fold assumes eval-mode, affine, track_running_stats BatchNorm and parameter invariance between build and run (guaranteed by this inference-only workload); guards skip any site not meeting these conditions, and each site folds independently, so a skipped site simply keeps its original conv+BN path.

The fused path activates only on the observed shape/stride/dtype/device signature; any other input, or calls with extra args/kwargs, fall back to the module's original bound forward with original parameters, preserving exact parent semantics for unobserved inputs (e.g., a hypothetical different batch shape).

Peak-memory reporting: the resident folded weights add ~45 MiB to allocated memory; this workload's objective is latency_ms, but the framework's peak-memory check will observe the increase (documented, not hidden).

No in-place rewrites: the model's parameters, buffers, module tree and autograd state are untouched, and inference-mode semantics are preserved (fused tensors are plain constants read inside inference_mode).
eliminated_calls_note: The first 20 IDs are the Conv2d module calls, the next 20 the BatchNorm2d module calls, and the last 5 the aten.batch_norm.default functional calls (20, 5, 5, 5, 5 observed invocations respectively). All are sub-calls of the 20 replaced ResNetConvLayer/ResNetShortCut forwards and no longer execute there; their consumers receive the fused output, which matches the original chain's output in shape/dtype/device/contiguity and value within FP32 rounding. The 11 aten.conv2d.default call IDs in the selection (6aaa41faeffad22146fd6761, 820dd67ec66704c34fdb68ec, 85e362c8893edef501c6b5c8, 02d936813f334fab42c607bc, adbd685b076c18d8d4f9ec07, 52801fdcf001973dc9b22a3b, fd7092acaf0a171825d76990, 2ee8fbf1c8409ad6a4a204cc, bcb576ff7b303e075fb61f51, c2db48d097463651f51bd75c, b892b0805dadd050499e86e1) are NOT eliminated: all 20 convolutions still execute per forward via F.conv2d inside the replacements, with unchanged signatures.
